articles.title: Jürgen Klopp disgusted by claims his Germany team are ‘not white enough’
articles.summary: He says social media claims are ‘nonsense’ and ‘idiocy’ Manager sees ‘no reason to pay attention to these people’ Jürgen Klopp has reacted with disgust to a social media debate questioning whether the Germany team he is in the process of forming are “white enough”.
body: Klopp said he believed there was no point in giving room to “such people and their utterances”, dismissing them as “complete nonsense”.

Asked in a press conference to respond to the debate as to whether the national team were “not German enough” or “not white enough”, he said: “There is absolutely no reason to pay attention to these people. You won’t get my thoughts on this. I have little time in everyday life for idiocy – and even less on social media.
“The great crux of our lives is that everyone is allowed to express their opinion … it’s insane when something like that exists.”

Klopp said that watching sportspeople interact with each other was proof to him that mutual respect was still possible. “The world could learn a thing or two from a sports changing room … There, everyone is respected based on the facts and not discredited based on false opinions. Full stop.”

articles.title: US soccer’s youth system is expensive, chaotic and overdue for reform
articles.summary: World Cup setbacks have renewed concern over America’s costly, fragmented youth system. The real test is whether the urgency survives the next news cycle. A few years ago, the idea that the US soccer community at large was neglecting youth soccer was met with silence or ridicule.
body: At a May 2022 conference call announcing a new collective bargaining agreement that effectively ended the “equal pay” saga, players were asked how they would build bridges with grassroots organizers who, in a fit of anger over perceived slights, nearly restored Carlos Cordeiro to US Soccer’s presidency not long after he resigned under heavy pressure. They could have offered any vague platitudes about how they valued youth and amateur soccer. They fell silent.

Meanwhile, in the social media sphere, suggestions that US Soccer should be paying its able-bodied national teams a bit less and redistributing more resources to development – as is the case in more successful soccer countries – found a hostile reception. The heavily memed Simpsons reference “Won’t somebody please think of the children?!” was a typical sarcastic response.

Today, everyone’s thinking of the children. But the thoughts are as chaotic and self-contradictory in the soccer world as they were when Helen Lovejoy squealed out her “think of the children” plea repeatedly on The Simpsons.
points: World Cup setbacks have renewed concern over America’s costly, fragmented youth system.
The real test is whether the urgency survives the next news cycle.
A few years ago, the idea that the US soccer community at large was neglecting youth soccer was met with silence or ridicule.
They could have offered any vague platitudes about how they valued youth and amateur soccer.

articles.title: England call up Crane and rest Archer for Pakistan series
articles.summary: Leg-spinner Mason Crane has the chance to play for England for the first time in eight years after being recalled for the one-day international tri-series in Pakistan.
body: The 29-year-old won his only Test cap against Australia in Sydney in 2018 and is now given an opportunity in the series which also involves Sri Lanka next month.
Crane, who also played two T20 internationals in 2017, could also push his case in the fight to be England's number one spinner in Test cricket.
Sam Curran and Adil Rashid both return after injuries, and uncapped pair James Coles and Henry Crocombe are included.
Jos Buttler is out with the hamstring injury he sustained last week, while Jacob Bethell is continuing his recovery from knee surgery.

articles.title: ‘Is there still a glass ceiling? Of course’: Kazim-Richards fights for breakthrough at Crawley
articles.summary: Alongside his assistant, Julian Gray, rookie manager talks about the state of play for black coaches and trying to lift his club off the bottom of League Two. Colin Kazim-Richards accepts the scale of the task of improving the situation at Crawley who sit bottom of League Two after seven games.
body: On a late summer’s afternoon at Crawley’s training ground in Sussex, Kazim-Richards, alongside his assistant, Julian Gray, the pair arriving in April and managing to save the club from relegation to the National League on the final day, speaks of the challenges ahead and how the team’s league position tells only part of the story.

“The results are not showing the work we’ve done; it’s more a case of when the process is going to start showing,” Kazim-Richards says. “We’ve got 16 new players, eight, nine debuts and different connections. So loads of ins, loads of outs and trying to get over the mentality of last season. It’s not a task that is just a week, two weeks or a three-week process.

“As players you don’t really understand what it entails as a manager. You’re trying to churn out results within trying to do the process you want. The recruitment, gelling people character-wise, mentality-wise, implementing a new structure, implementing a new standard within the club, and not just the football side. But it ultimately falls down on the results. We know that and it’s something we’re working to change.”

articles.title: Pleasant surprises of the NFL season so far: Brock Purdy for MVP and actual Raiders competence
articles.summary: It’s still early in the 2026 season but a number of teams and players have found unexpected levels of success in the last few weeks. Last season ended with a Super Bowl in which neither team – the Seattle Seahawks and the New England Patriots – had been expected to participate.
body: It’s early to state which surprises will be the most fun to recall this time around, but here are four to watch as things progress.

Under an obscure Santa Clara bylaw, we are legally obliged to point out that Purdy has outplayed his status as the last pick in the 2022 draft. But last season, the San Francisco 49ers quarterback was caught up in his team’s horrible injury luck ( which continues unabated ), missing eight games. Purdy still played well when healthy, but nobody was quite prepared for how good he has been in 2026.

The 49ers are 3-0 despite all the injury hits, and Purdy is the primary reason. He has completed 60 of 83 passes (72.3%) for 789 yards (9.5 yards per attempt), nine touchdowns, one interception, no sacks, and a passer rating of 133.1, which leads the league quite comfortably (in second place is Drew Lock, more on which later).

articles.title: Curtis shines as revamped Scotland youth set-up begins
articles.summary: Amidst a raft of coaching changes in Scotland's youth set up, the under-21s delivered an eye-catching display, with Rangers winger Findlay Curtis at the heart of it.
body: As starts to a new era go, Scotland Under-21s' dominant 5-2 defeat of Azerbaijan was a rousing one.
Findlay Curtis ran riot, Tyler Fletcher cruised through the game in midfield and three strikers all scored.
All of that contributed to a fantastic team performance full of attacking elan and aggressive pressing.

It was exactly the type of display new head coach Tony Docherty and his assistant Steven Naismith demanded after replacing Scot Gemmill, who had been in charge of Scotland's best young talent for the past decade.

articles.title: 'I kept fighting right to the end' - emotional Nishikori retires
articles.summary: A tearful Kei Nishikori says he "kept fighting right to the end" as the former world number four ends his professional career at the Japan Open.
body: Nishikori, known as one of the best players to never win a Grand Slam, lost 6-4 6-4 to world number eight Frances Tiafoe in Tokyo.
The 36-year-old became the first Japanese man to reach a major final when he faced Marin Cilic in the 2014 US Open showpiece.
Nishikori beat then world number one Novak Djokovic on his way to the New York final and defeated Rafael Nadal for Olympic bronze at the 2016 Games in Rio.
"Playing in Japan is always a special moment," an emotional Nishikori told his home crowd.

articles.title: Cove consider options after transfer ban imposed
articles.summary: Cove Rangers are "considering all available options" after having a season-long registration ban imposed upon them by the SPFL over rule breaches.
body: The league body say the Scottish League 1 club admitted "failing to make a historic contractual payment to a player when due and then failed to notify the SPFL that it had been in default of that rule".
"The club was also found to have provided incorrect information to the SPFL when it certified that it had no overdue payables to current or former players as at 31 January 2026," the SPFL said.
"Following these rule breaches by the club, the tribunal imposed a registration embargo which will remain in place until 31 May 2027 and a fine of £5,000 (£2,000 of which is suspended).
Paul Hartley's Cove are second bottom of League 1, a point above Queen of the South, after picking up five points from their opening eight fixtures.

articles.title: Parma midfielder Mandela Keita reveals he could have joined African nation prior to Belgian recall
articles.summary: Mandela Keita is back in the Belgian fold after a few years on the sidelines. The Parma midfielder reunited with his former head coach at Antwerp during the recent international window, with Mark van Bommel immediately including Keita in the squad.
body: However, during his time out of the Belgian national team, another country came calling. Mandela is eligible to represent Guinea as well as Belgium, and the West African nation was keen to take advantage of his lack of opportunities with the Red Devils. However, in an interview with HLN, the Parma midfielder revealed that he never considered changing his international allegiance. Keita said ‘I have dual nationality and they contacted me. But my focus was always on the Red Devils. It never crossed my mind to switch ‘. His decision to stay the course has now been rewarded with a return to the Red Devils set up.

During his time at Antwerp, Keita and van Bommel won the Belgian Pro League in 2023 alongside the Belgian cup. This season of success earned Keita a first Belgian call up that same year. However, Keita was then ignored by the Belgian national team until van Bommel was appointed. In that time, he left Belgian football to join Parma in Serie A. Since 2024, Keita has played 77 games for the Italian side, scoring one goal and providing two assists.

articles.title: Mike Brown explains new roles for Karl Anthony-Towns and OG Anunoby in the Knicks offense
articles.summary: The New York Knicks will have a target on their back this season as the defending champions, but head coach Mike Brown is ready with plans of his own. The New York Knicks won the NBA championship thanks to their elite roster and incredible teamwork.
body: Going into the 2026-27 season, many teams will be focused on the Knicks, trying to stop them and beat them. It is only a natural part of the process.

As such, the coaching staff led by head coach Mike Brown have to figure out how to change things around. The coach has some ideas already, especially on the offensive side of the ball. He spoke about a few of those with the media recently.
OG Anunoby’s tip-in to win a game in the NBA Finals might be the most iconic moment of that Knicks championship. His versatility was pivotal in helping New York reach the promised land.

It is no wonder then, that Brown is already thinking about different ways to use Anunoby in this coming season. It isn’t just him either, the coach spoke about the various ideas the team will implement which involved Karl-Anthony Towns and Mikal Bridges.

articles.title: Rashid, Curran return from injury as England rest Archer for ODI tri-series
articles.summary: Adil Rashid and Sam Curran have been recalled to England's ODI squad after recovering from injury, but Jofra Archer will be rested for the tri-series against Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
body: Three uncapped players are included in the 16-player squad for the series in Pakistan, which will see Harry Brook's side play each opponent twice. Spinner Mason Crane is included eight years on from making his last international appearance, which came in the final Test of England's 2017/18 Ashes tour.
Sussex duo James Coles and Henry Crocombe could also make their ODI debuts having been included after being part of England's white-ball squads earlier this summer.
Rashid featured as England beat Sri Lanka in a home T20 series in September but the spinner then missed the ODI matches that followed because of a hand injury.
Curran had appeared to be in contention for a first Test appearance since 2021 before his summer was ended by groin surgery in August, but the all-rounder is on track to be ready to play in Pakistan.

articles.title: 'It looked bleak - but Vrancken has been brilliant'
articles.summary: We asked you to rate Hearts' season and tell us what Wouter Vrancken should be focusing on during the international break. Here are some of your comments: Simon: Hearts' season has gone roughly as I expected. Massive influx of new players, new manager with a different style.
body: Derek: A lot more positive than I thought it was going to be - gutted midfield, new manager, talisman gone, gubbed by Graz, it looked bleak. Vrancken has turned out to be brilliant, he plays attacking football, and it's been a nervy joy to watch. If we get the defence sorted we could really be on to something this season, especially since the Old Firm are still nothing to fear. A cup semi-final against Hibs is mouthwateringly exciting and there's far more positives than negatives so far.

Alasdair: Unreal going forward but hapless in defence - If Wouter can stop us shipping stupid goals from simple balls over the top we could be on for a great season but time will tell. High risk, high reward but the defence really needs sorted.

Chris: The sheer effort required to qualify for Europe took its toll and it's unfortunate we didn't strengthen the defence before the window closed - despite being exceptionally thin on the ground. The international break is fantastic for us to allow players to rest up and get ready for another busy few months of football!

articles.title: 'Point fingers somewhere else!' - Hamilton backs Vasseur but calls for other Ferrari change
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton has launched an impassioned defence of Frederic Vasseur as Ferrari's team principal and suggested he would like to instead see other structural changes at the team.
body: Hamilton was speaking two days after Ferrari took the unusual step of arranging a media briefing for journalists in which a spokesperson said the company's management retained "full confidence" in Vasseur in the wake of growing speculation around the Frenchman's position in the team principal role amid a run of five races without a podium.

Speaking ahead of this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Hamilton welcomed Ferrari's public move to silence the recent noise around the team - external criticism and speculation which the Briton said was "trying to break our spirit" but "not succeeding".
"I think it's good that they did it," said Hamilton of Ferrari's support of Vasseur.

"In terms of how it unifies the team, I think we already were unified. Honestly, outside sources seem to be so negative towards us as a team and be trying to break our spirit but they are not succeeding.

articles.title: 'A risk not worth taking' - PL execs not expecting clubs to vote for Man City expulsion
articles.summary: Two senior executives at different top-level Premier League clubs have told Sky Sports News they would be "staggered" and "amazed" if 15 clubs were prepared to vote to expel Manchester City from the league, with such a move akin to a "self-inflicted commercial disaster".
body: Expulsion is one of several punishments available to the independent commission, which earlier this week found Man City guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought against them over alleged financial mismanagement. Other potential sanctions include a fine, a points deduction and/or a transfer embargo.
Man City remain adamant they are innocent and have vowed to fight the judgement.

Sky Sports News has been told discussions remain ongoing within, and between, the bosses of other clubs in the Premier League about how they might react to developments, with a number of them considering their own legal positions in terms of a possible financial claim against Man City.

But in a new and surprising development, we have been told that many rival clubs consider Man City such a key part of the commercial attraction of the Premier League, both in the UK and globally, that if rival clubs voted to expel them, it would be as if those clubs were "cutting off their noses to spite their faces".
